cosy-lesson.title: "I have no special talents, I am only passionately curious.": Albert Einstein

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Talent – a natural ability to do something well.

p.em: Example: She has a great talent for learning languages.

cosy-blockquote.p: Passion – a strong feeling of excitement or interest in something.

p.em: Example: He has a deep passion for science and nature.

cosy-blockquote.p: Special – different from what is normal or usual.

p.em: Example: You do not need special skills to begin your learning journey.

cosy-blockquote.p: Curious – wanting to know or learn about something.

p.em: Example: Young children are always curious about the world.

cosy-blockquote.p: Skill – an ability to do something well because you practiced it.

p.em: Example: Speaking another language is an important skill today.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ordinary – normal or usual; not special.

p.em: Example: He was an ordinary boy who worked very hard every day.

cosy-blockquote.p: Knowledge – information and understanding that you get from study.

p.em: Example: Reading books is a great way to get knowledge.

cosy-blockquote.p: Simple – easy to understand or do; not complex.

p.em: Example: The teacher gave a simple explanation of the grammar rule.

cosy-blockquote.p: Focus – to give all your attention to one activity.

p.em: Example: It is important to focus on your personal goals.

cosy-blockquote.p: Humble – not proud; not thinking you are better than others.

p.em: Example: Despite his great success, the scientist remained very humble.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Do you believe that having a natural talent is more important than practicing hard?
★ Do you have a special talent that you are proud of?

How does a deep passion help you when your studies become difficult?
★ What is your biggest passion in life right now?

Why do we often think that famous scientists have a special brain?
★ Is there a special hobby you would like to start this year?

In what ways does being curious make your daily life more exciting?
★ What is something you are very curious about today?

What is the most useful skill you have learned outside of school?
★ What is a skill you would like to learn in the future?

Can an ordinary person achieve great success with only curiosity?
★ Do you prefer a quiet, ordinary day or an exciting one?

How does getting new knowledge change the way we see the world?
★ What kind of knowledge do you enjoy sharing with others?

Why is it sometimes difficult to find a simple answer to a question?
★ What is a simple thing that always makes you happy?

How do you stay and maintain your focus when there are many distractions around you?
★ Where do you go when you need to focus on your work?

Why is it important for very successful people to remain humble?
★ Who is the most humble person you know, and what did they teach you?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: Which quality is most important for achieving great success in these different fields? Rank them: - 🎨 Fields of Art & Music Does a great artist need natural talent, or do they just need to practice patiently? - 🔬 Fields of Science & Logic Is deep curiosity the most important skill for a scientist, or do they need a special brain? - 🗣️ Learning Foreign Languages Do you need a special talent for grammar, or do you just need to focus passionately? - 💼 Building a Successful Business Is focus and passion more important, or do you need special wealth and connections?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will allow us to measure a child's natural talent at birth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you feel if your future career was decided by your early special talents?

Modern digital screens will eventually destroy our collective capacity for deep passion and focus. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use smart apps to help you stay focus on your personal projects?

Future schools will completely ban exams, letting children learn purely based on their curious interests. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think future kids will be more curious than today's children?

As artificial intelligence advances, humans will not need to learn any complex skill. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What is one simple skill you hope humans never lose?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our willingness to live ordinary, simple lives. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where ordinary lives are seen as boring?

In the coming decades, human knowledge will double every single week. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send one piece of knowledge to people 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true simple living incredibly difficult to maintain. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic city that guarantees a simple lifestyle at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for focus rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope focus will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A future world governed fully by smart technology will leave no space left for the quiet beauty of being humble. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If an app could make you very successful, would you still remain humble?

One day, being passionately curious will be seen as the single most valuable trait of any worker. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you want to show greater passion right now?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
